correctness.rationale: The transpose-times-itself identity for the random two-stage 2x2 update gives an exact scalar squared-norm multiplier; the joint Bernoulli table and outer independence yield the full mean-square law. Affinity in the unique coupling parameter proves global optimality. Strict positivity of the mixed fourth moment gives the if-and-only-if stability classification, and differentiation of its rational ceiling yields the exact frontier. All boundaries and example fractions were directly reconstructed; 2,467 standalone exact-rational checks supplement the universal analytic proof.

The prior implications inspected do not entail this optimized dependence.

originality.rationale: Inspected published primary arguments establish stochastic bilinear noise counterexamples, benefits of same-sample reuse, and convergence guarantees for same-sample or independent-sample extragradient, but not a sharp optimization over all joint couplings with fixed two-point stage marginals. The explicit anti-coupling stability rescue is not a corollary of the bounds inspected. Search absence alone does not establish priority; unindexed equivalent derivations remain possible.
residual_risks: Mathematically equivalent within-stage antithetic sampling formulas may exist in unindexed optimization literature; searches and inspected primary statements do not prove universal novelty.
The proof does not extend its if-and-only-if two-point optimality to nonbinary strengths, higher-dimensional games, distinct predictor/corrector steps, or nonstationary stage couplings.

value.rationale: Pairwise sampling dependence is a design choice at fixed oracle marginals and cost. The theorem proves a sharp endogenous reversal in which dependency is best, and a natural interpolation benchmark (strengths 1,2 with balanced marginals) where the unconventional antithetic rule converges in mean square but conventional same-sample and independent rules diverge. It also identifies the exact parameter condition when anticorrelation increases the maximum stable step; this is a complete natural structural stability classification, not a renaming or recomputation of a known table.
